title: HBM4 Evidence Release 001
description: Research-candidate findings and proposed Atlas relationships for HBM3E, HBM4 and HBM4E. Nothing in this file is a published Atlas relationship; every candidate requires named human review against the cited passages before it may be moved into data/dependency-atlas.json.
rights_note: Classification, analysis and arithmetic are original project work by AIElectronicChips.com (Sohadot). Quoted passages are short excerpts (at most 20 words each, 40 per citation) reproduced for citation and verification; the underlying texts, specifications and standards remain the property of their publishers. No endorsement by JEDEC or any company is implied. This file is a research candidate: it is visible in the public repository but is excluded from the published website.

findings.statement: JEDEC's 2025-04-16 announcement of JESD270-4 (HBM4) states transfer speeds up to 8 Gb/s across a 2048-bit interface, for total bandwidth up to 2 TB/s.

evidence.locator: "With transfer speeds up to 8 Gb/s across a 2048-bit interface, HBM4 boosts total bandwidth up to 2 TB/s."

findings.scope: Industry standard as announced; not a statement about shipped products
limitations: Read from a syndicated copy of JEDEC's Business Wire release; jedec.org itself was not reachable
Announcement only: the normative JESD270-4 / JESD270-4A document has not been reviewed

findings.statement: JEDEC's HBM4 announcement states that independent channels per stack double from 16 (HBM3) to 32, with two pseudo-channels per channel.

evidence.locator: "from 16 channels (HBM3) to 32 channels with 2 pseudo-channels per channel"

limitations: Read from a syndicated copy of JEDEC's Business Wire release; jedec.org itself was not reachable
Announcement only: the normative JESD270-4 / JESD270-4A document has not been reviewed

findings.statement: JEDEC's HBM4 announcement lists 4-high, 8-high, 12-high and 16-high DRAM stack configurations with 24 Gb or 32 Gb die densities, providing a cube density of 64GB (32 Gb, 16-high).

evidence.locator: "4-high, 8-high, 12-high and 16-high DRAM stack configurations with 24 Gb or 32 Gb die densities"; "a higher cube density of 64GB (32 Gb 16-High)"

findings.scope: Industry standard as announced; permitted configurations, not products offered
limitations: Read from a syndicated copy of JEDEC's Business Wire release; jedec.org itself was not reachable
Announcement only: the normative JESD270-4 / JESD270-4A document has not been reviewed
A permitted configuration is not evidence that any supplier offers it

findings.statement: JEDEC's HBM4 announcement states backward compatibility with existing HBM3 controllers, allowing a single controller to work with both if needed, and Directed Refresh Management (DRFM) for improved row-hammer mitigation and RAS.

evidence.locator: "backwards compatibility with existing HBM3 controllers"; "allowing a single controller to work with both HBM3 and HBM4 if needed"; "Directed Refresh Management (DRFM) for improved row-hammer mitigation"

limitations: Read from a syndicated copy of JEDEC's Business Wire release; jedec.org itself was not reachable
Announcement only: the normative JESD270-4 / JESD270-4A document has not been reviewed
Controller compatibility does not imply drop-in substitution at the package or platform level

findings.statement: JEDEC's HBM4 announcement states that JESD270-4 supports vendor-specific VDDQ levels of 0.7 V, 0.75 V, 0.8 V or 0.9 V and VDDC levels of 1.0 V or 1.05 V, which it associates with lower power consumption.

evidence.locator: "vendor specific VDDQ (0.7V, 0.75V, 0.8V or 0.9V) and VDDC (1.0V or 1.05V) levels"; "resulting in lower power consumption"

limitations: Read from a syndicated copy of JEDEC's Business Wire release; jedec.org itself was not reachable
Announcement only: the normative JESD270-4 / JESD270-4A document has not been reviewed
The announcement gives no power figures; which levels any supplier uses is not stated

findings.statement: SK hynix reports that its HBM4 doubles bandwidth through 2,048 I/O terminals and operates at over 10 Gbps, which it contrasts with a JEDEC standard operating speed of 8 Gbps.

evidence.locator: "the bandwidth doubled through adoption of 2,048 I/O terminals"; "over 10Gbps"; "far exceeded the JEDEC* standard operating speed(8Gbps)"

limitations: Company-reported speed; no independent measurement
No absolute per-stack bandwidth figure is given

findings.statement: Micron reported shipping 36GB 12-high HBM4 samples in June 2025 with a 2048-bit interface, greater than 2.0 TB/s per stack, built on its 1-beta DRAM process.

evidence.locator: "Micron HBM4 features a 2048-bit interface, achieving speeds greater than 2.0 TB/s per memory stack"; "Built on its well-established 1ß (1-beta) DRAM process"

limitations: Bandwidth basis per footnote is internal Micron testing
Sample stage only

evidence.locator: "With HBM4, Micron achieves over 11 Gb/s pin speeds"; "enabling a bandwidth greater than 2.8 TB/s"

limitations: Footnote: internal testing and confidential customer test-vehicle validation
Does not restate interface width or DRAM process

findings.statement: Samsung reported on 2026-02-12 that its HBM4 runs at a consistent 11.7 Gbps, about 46% above the 8 Gbps industry standard, can be enhanced to 13 Gbps, and reaches a maximum of 3.3 TB/s per stack (2.7x HBM3E). It said data I/Os double from 1,024 to 2,048 and that the core uses its 1c DRAM process.

evidence.locator: "consistent processing speed of 11.7 gigabits-per-second (Gbps)"; "exceeding the industry standard of 8Gbps by approximately 46%"; "increased by 2.7x compared to HBM3E, to a maximum of 3.3 terabytes-per-second (TB/s)"; "doubling of data I/Os from 1,024 to 2,048 pins"
"sixth-generation 10-nanometer (nm)-class DRAM process (1c)"; "can be enhanced to 13Gbps"

limitations: Company-reported figures; the release gives no test conditions or footnotes
'Maximum' bandwidth is stated without the pin rate it applies to

findings.statement: Samsung reported offering HBM4 in 12-layer capacities from 24GB to 36GB, with 16-layer stacking planned to expand offerings to up to 48GB, and a 4nm logic base die.

evidence.locator: "Samsung offers HBM4 in capacities ranging from 24 gigabytes (GB) to 36GB"; "16-layer stacking, which will expand offerings to up to 48GB"; "4nm logic base die"

limitations: 16-layer HBM4 is a stated plan, not a reported shipment
The release does not say which plant or business unit makes the base die

findings.statement: Samsung reported shipping 12-layer, 48GB HBM4E samples in May 2026 with a stable 14 Gbps pin speed scalable to 16 Gbps and up to 3.6 TB/s per stack.

evidence.locator: "begun shipping the industry's first 12-layer HBM4E samples"; "offered in a 48-gigabyte (GB) capacity"; "a stable pin speed of 14 gigabits-per-second (Gbps)"; "scalable up to 16Gbps"; "up to 3.6 terabytes-per-second (TB/s) per stack"

limitations: Sample stage only
HBM4E I/O count is not stated
No JEDEC HBM4E document is cited

findings.statement: Per-stack bandwidth equals interface width times per-pin rate divided by eight. At 2,048 bits, 8 Gb/s gives 2.05 TB/s, 10 Gb/s gives 2.56 TB/s, 11 Gb/s gives 2.82 TB/s, 13 Gb/s gives 3.33 TB/s, 14 Gb/s gives 3.58 TB/s and 16 Gb/s gives 4.10 TB/s. Every disclosed vendor figure is arithmetically consistent with a 2,048-bit interface, including Samsung's HBM4E figures, whose release gives no I/O count. Samsung's HBM4 maximum of 3.3 TB/s matches its 13 Gb/s enhanced rate, not its 11.7 Gb/s consistent rate (3.00 TB/s). For HBM3E, 1,024 bits at Samsung's stated 9.6 Gb/s gives 1.23 TB/s, consistent with Samsung's 2.7x multiple and Micron's cited 1.2 TB/s.

evidence.locator: "transfer speeds up to 8 Gb/s across a 2048-bit interface"
"over 11 Gb/s pin speeds"; "greater than 2.8 TB/s"
"14 gigabits-per-second"; "up to 3.6 terabytes-per-second (TB/s) per stack"
HBM4E: "16Gbps per pin and 4.0 terabytes-per-second (TB/s) bandwidth"
"to a maximum of 3.3 terabytes-per-second (TB/s)"; "maximum pin speed of 9.6Gbps of its predecessor, HBM3E"; "2.7x"
footnote: "published HBM3E specifications (2.0 TB/s vs. 1.2 TB/s)"

findings.scope: Arithmetic on disclosed figures; decimal terabytes
limitations: Consistency is not proof that HBM4E keeps a 2,048-bit interface
Peak interface bandwidth is not sustained application bandwidth
assumptions: All 2,048 data bits transfer at the stated per-pin rate
Samsung does not state which pin rate its 3.3 TB/s maximum corresponds to; matching it to 13 Gb/s is arithmetic, not a Samsung statement

evidence.locator: "with plans to expand the lineup to include 32GB (8-layer) and 64GB (16-layer) configurations"

findings.statement: Dividing disclosed stack capacity by layer count gives 3 GB (24 Gb) per DRAM die for 36GB 12-high and 48GB 16-high HBM4, and 4 GB (32 Gb) per die for Samsung's 48GB 12-layer HBM4E and its planned 64GB 16-layer part. Both densities match the 24 Gb and 32 Gb options in JEDEC's HBM4 announcement.

evidence.locator: "12-layer"; "36GB"
"HBM4 48GB 16H"
"48-gigabyte (GB) capacity"; "64GB (16-layer)"
"24 Gb or 32 Gb die densities"

The base die contributes no user-addressable capacity
GB is 2^30-style binary gigabytes as used for DRAM capacity

findings.statement: HBM4 base dies are now made in three different ways among the suppliers reviewed. SK hynix planned to use TSMC's advanced logic process (2024 plan, not restated in later reviewed sources); Samsung states a 4nm logic process, which its HBM4E release attributes to Samsung Foundry; Micron states its base logic die is designed and manufactured in-house. Where the base die comes from a logic foundry, HBM4 supply depends on logic-wafer fabrication as well as DRAM fabrication; the dependency is external for SK hynix, intra-company for Samsung and, as disclosed, internal to Micron's own manufacturing. SK hynix states only that its base dies up to HBM3E used its own proprietary technology; that HBM4 marks a new dependency is our inference.

evidence.locator: "plans to adopt TSMC’s advanced logic process for HBM4’s base die"
"N12 and N3 logic base die for HBM4"
"Samsung Foundry's 4nm logic base die"
"4nm logic process for HBM4"
"on the base logic die and DRAM core dies, which are designed and manufactured in-house"

findings.statement: If Rubin's 288 GB is built from 36GB 12-high HBM4 stacks, it uses eight stacks. NVIDIA's 22 TB/s peak then implies about 2.75 TB/s per stack (about 10.7 Gb/s per pin at 2,048 bits); the 19.2 TB/s figure in NVIDIA's 2026-11-05 article implies about 2.4 TB/s per stack (about 9.4 Gb/s per pin). Both exceed JEDEC's announced 8 Gb/s baseline, which shows the platform relies on above-baseline HBM4 speed grades.

evidence.locator: "up to 288 GB of HBM4"; "12-Hi stacks"; "up to 22 TB/s"
"HBM4 36GB 12H"
"12-layer"; "36GB"
"transfer speeds up to 8 Gb/s"
"bandwidth rose to 19.2 TB/s"

limitations: NVIDIA does not state the stack count
Which of the two bandwidth figures is current is unresolved
assumptions: Each 12-high HBM4 stack is 36GB, as SK hynix and Micron disclose for 12-high HBM4
All stacks run at the same rate

findings.statement: Micron and Samsung each state that their HBM4 is designed for NVIDIA Vera Rubin, so the platform is designed to accept HBM4 from more than one supplier. "designed for the" NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform

unresolved.question: What do the normative JESD270-4 and JESD270-4A documents specify beyond the announcement, including timing, any speed bins above 8 Gb/s and the revision-A changes?
unresolved.why_unresolved: JEDEC's 2025-04-16 announcement has now been read through a Business Wire syndication, but an announcement summarises a standard. The JESD270-4 and JESD270-4A documents themselves have not been reviewed.
unresolved.next_evidence_needed: A reviewer reads the JESD270-4A document from JEDEC before any normative statement is made.

unresolved.question: Has JEDEC published an HBM4E standard, and what parameters does it define?
unresolved.why_unresolved: No reviewed source cites a JEDEC HBM4E document; Samsung's HBM4E release cites none.
unresolved.next_evidence_needed: JEDEC publication record or committee statement.

unresolved.question: What process node is Micron's in-house HBM4 base logic die built on?
unresolved.why_unresolved: Micron's FY2026 10-K states the base logic die is designed and manufactured in-house using advanced CMOS, but gives no node. Its press releases do not mention the base die.
unresolved.next_evidence_needed: A Micron technical disclosure or filing naming the base logic die's process node.

unresolved.question: Does SK hynix's production HBM4 use a TSMC-made logic base die, and on which node?
unresolved.why_unresolved: The 2024 MOU states a plan. SK hynix's later reviewed releases do not restate it, the portion of its July 2026 prospectus read defines custom HBM by base-die integration but names no manufacturer or process, and TSMC does not name customers.
unresolved.next_evidence_needed: SK hynix or TSMC disclosure tying the production base die to a named node.

unresolved.question: What is each supplier's HBM4 production capacity, yield and customer allocation?
unresolved.why_unresolved: No reviewed primary source quantifies them; 'mass', 'large-scale' and 'high-volume' production are unquantified.
unresolved.next_evidence_needed: Audited filings with segment or product-level disclosure; this project will not estimate it.

unresolved.question: Which suppliers' HBM4 is qualified for which accelerator platforms, and at what speed grade?
unresolved.why_unresolved: 'Designed for' statements are not qualification disclosures. Micron reports high-volume HBM4 shipments for one unnamed lead customer and qualification samples shipped to multiple end-customers; no supplier reports completed qualification by named platform.
unresolved.next_evidence_needed: Platform-vendor or supplier disclosure of completed qualification.

unresolved.question: Is Rubin's per-GPU HBM4 bandwidth 22 TB/s or 19.2 TB/s?
unresolved.why_unresolved: NVIDIA's dated articles give 'aggregate bandwidth of up to 22 TB/s' (2026-01-05) and 'up to 22 TB/s of peak bandwidth' (2026-07-21), then an unqualified 'bandwidth rose to 19.2 TB/s' (2026-11-05). Current undated product pages still disagree: Vera Rubin NVL72 lists 19.2 TB/s per GPU (1,400 TB/s per rack); HGX lists 22 TB/s per GPU. No page labels either figure preliminary, projected or subject to change, and none explains the difference. A later revision, a configuration difference and a peak-versus-rated distinction all remain possible; none is established.
unresolved.next_evidence_needed: A dated NVIDIA datasheet or specification note that states per-GPU memory bandwidth and the configuration or conditions it applies to.

unresolved.question: What are the thermal limits of 16-high HBM4 stacks, and does reaching them require hybrid bonding?
unresolved.why_unresolved: Samsung presents hybrid copper bonding as a future method; Micron is sampling 16-high HBM4 without disclosing its stacking method; no reviewed source establishes a requirement.
unresolved.next_evidence_needed: Peer-reviewed or supplier technical paper on 16-high HBM4 thermal behaviour and bonding.

unresolved.question: Which interposer or bridge technology, substrate and assembly providers do HBM4 accelerator packages depend on?
unresolved.why_unresolved: Reviewed sources describe CoWoS generally and do not identify per-product interposer type, substrate suppliers or assembly sites.
unresolved.next_evidence_needed: Foundry, OSAT and substrate-supplier disclosures tied to HBM4 products.

unresolved.question: How are HBM4 stacks tested before integration (known-good-stack), and who performs that testing?
unresolved.why_unresolved: No reviewed primary source addresses HBM4 test flows.

unresolved.question: What is the status and scope of JEDEC's reduced-pin-count SPHBM4 effort?
unresolved.why_unresolved: The JEDEC page could not be retrieved; only a search-index summary was seen, which is not used as evidence.

candidate_nodes.description: The bottom die of an HBM stack carrying the interface and control logic, made on a logic process for HBM4 by suppliers that disclose it.

candidate_nodes.label: Advanced logic foundry process
candidate_nodes.description: Logic wafer fabrication at nodes such as 12nm-class, 4nm-class or 3nm-class, as offered by logic foundries.

candidate_nodes.label: CoWoS
candidate_nodes.description: TSMC's Chip on Wafer on Substrate advanced-packaging family, used to place logic dies and HBM stacks in one package.

candidate_nodes.label: NVIDIA Rubin GPU
candidate_nodes.description: NVIDIA accelerator generation disclosed with up to 288 GB of HBM4.

candidate_relationships.statement: HBM stacks core DRAM dies on a TSV-bearing base die; for HBM4, SK hynix planned a logic-process base die, Samsung states a 4nm logic base die, and Micron states its base logic die is made in-house.
candidate_relationships.temporal_scope: Disclosures dated 2024-04-19 to 2026-09-03 (Micron fiscal year end)
limitations: SK hynix statement is an MOU-stage plan
Micron does not state its base die's process node

candidate_relationships.statement: TSMC lists N12 and N3 logic base dies for HBM4, and SK hynix planned to use TSMC's advanced logic process for its HBM4 base die.
candidate_relationships.geographic_scope: TSMC offering and SK hynix plan only; does not hold for Micron, which reports in-house base logic die manufacture
limitations: Does not establish which shipping products use which node
Micron's FY2026 10-K reports in-house manufacture of its HBM4 base logic die, so this relationship is not industry-wide
No capacity or allocation inference

candidate_relationships.statement: TSMC describes CoWoS as advancing to meet AI demand for logic and HBM, planning 12 or more HBM stacks per package with 9.5-reticle CoWoS in 2027; SK hynix aimed to optimise its HBM integration with CoWoS.
candidate_relationships.geographic_scope: TSMC packaging offering; not the only HBM integration route
candidate_relationships.temporal_scope: Disclosures dated 2024-04-19 and 2025-04-23; 2027 plan is forward-looking
limitations: Other packaging providers and routes are not assessed
The 2027 volume-production plan is not a verified outcome

candidate_relationships.statement: NVIDIA states Rubin integrates up to 288 GB of HBM4 on 12-Hi stacks; Micron and Samsung each state their HBM4 is designed for NVIDIA Vera Rubin.
limitations: Per-GPU bandwidth conflict between NVIDIA's own dated articles (22 vs 19.2 TB/s) is unresolved
Supplier qualification and share are not established
